bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / exact staged vulnerable source / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer at `src/core/parser/parse_addr_spec.c:228` while parsing the staged 17-byte witness (`gt_results/arvo_38080/poc`, sha256 `4a533f7db1f5acac622c49a8c5637a61d87f5e1264e00dcead3b0256aa97b534`). The saved stack proves that the message parser admits the input far enough to reach `get_hdr_field()` on a compact `T:` header, then `parse_addr_spec()` stops at the semicolon in that header body and calls `parse_to_param()` on the attacker-controlled suffix starting there. Inside `parse_to_param()`, the semicolon starts a new parameter, the following byte is accepted as a one-byte parameter name, `=` moves the state machine to `S_PARA_VALUE`, and `"` moves it to `PARA_VALUE_QUOTED`. The witness then supplies three spaces and a final backslash as the last byte of the whole buffer. In the vulnerable source, entering the quoted-value escape branch at that final backslash checks only `status == PARA_VALUE_QUOTED`; it does not verify `tmp + 1 < end` before executing `switch(*(tmp + 1))`. Because `tmp == end - 1` for the witnessed trailing backslash, the next line reads one byte at `end`, matching ASan's `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `parse_to_param -> parse_addr_spec -> parse_to`. The patch expresses the missing obligation by adding `if(tmp+1>=end)` before this escape read and before the opening-quote branch, but Stage 02 did not run the fixed image.

source.code:
to_b->body.len = tmp - to_b->body.s;
tmp = parse_to_param(tmp, end, to_b, allow_comma_sep, &saved_status);
source.description: First vulnerability-relevant project statement. When `parse_addr_spec` sees the attacker-controlled semicolon in the To-header body, it fixes the body length and hands the parameter substring plus the original buffer end pointer into `parse_to_param`.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_38080/poc` is 17 bytes (sha256 `4a533f7db1f5acac622c49a8c5637a61d87f5e1264e00dcead3b0256aa97b534`). In the crashing run, the only newline is followed by the compact header name `T:`, and this step calls `parse_to_param` with `tmp` at the semicolon before the suffix `;0xff=` plus an opening quote, three spaces, and a final backslash, while `end` still points one byte past that final backslash.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The quoted-value escape handler dereferences the byte after the current backslash even when the backslash is already the last byte in the buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/core/parser/parse_addr_spec.c:228:14` in `parse_to_param` and says the faulting address `0x603000000111` is 0 bytes to the right of the 17-byte input region `[0x603000000100, 0x603000000111)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The quoted-value escape branch is selected solely by parser state and has no end-of-buffer check before the following line reads `*(tmp + 1)`.
root_cause.note: For the witnessed input, the trailing backslash is the final byte, so entering this branch means `tmp == end - 1`. The fix adds the missing `if(tmp+1>=end)` guard immediately before the read, which is the source-level obligation absent in the vulnerable version.

tainted_value_origin.code:
to_b->body.len = tmp - to_b->body.s;
tmp = parse_to_param(tmp, end, to_b, allow_comma_sep, &saved_status);
tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker state is the parameter-parser input range: `tmp` points at the semicolon starting the To-header parameter section, and `end` remains one byte past the complete 17-byte fuzz buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The crashing witness reaches `parse_to_param` on the suffix `;0xff=` plus an opening quote, three spaces, and a final backslash.
tainted_value_origin.note: Every later parser-state transition and the final out-of-bounds read are computed relative to this `(tmp, end)` range.

parser_admitted.description: After header-name parsing identifies the compact `T:` form as a To header, `get_hdr_field` records the body start and dispatches the attacker-controlled body into the To parser.
parser_admitted.note: This admission point is source-grounded by `parse_hname2.c`, whose header-name table maps both `t` and `To` to `HDR_TO_T` at lines 123-124. The saved ASan stack then shows `get_hdr_field -> parse_to -> parse_addr_spec`.

fine_trace.code:
to_b->body.len = tmp - to_b->body.s;
tmp = parse_to_param(tmp, end, to_b, allow_comma_sep, &saved_status);
fine_trace.note: Source. After `get_hdr_field` has already dispatched the compact `T:` header body into the To parser, `parse_addr_spec` reaches the attacker-controlled semicolon in that body. This statement fixes the non-parameter body length and hands the parameter substring beginning at that semicolon, together with the unchanged `end` pointer for the whole 17-byte witness, into `parse_to_param`.

At the leading semicolon, `parse_to_param` starts a new general parameter record. The only vulnerability-relevant effect here is the state transition to `S_PARA_NAME`, which means the next attacker byte will be interpreted as the beginning of a parameter name.

The first byte after `;` is `0xff`. In state `S_PARA_NAME`, the default branch accepts that non-delimiter byte as the start of the parameter name by storing its address in `param->name.s` and switching the state machine to `PARA_NAME`.

When the parser reaches `=`, the one-byte name recorded in step 3 is closed and the state changes to `S_PARA_VALUE`. This state transition is what makes the following quote open a quoted value instead of being rejected as an unexpected character.

At the opening quote after `=`, the parser starts a quoted parameter value. It records the first byte after the quote as `param->value.s` and changes state to `PARA_VALUE_QUOTED`. The three following spaces in the witness do not change this state, so the parser remains in quoted-value mode until it reaches the final backslash.

Root cause. The witness ends with a backslash, so after the three quoted spaces from step 5 the loop reaches this branch with `tmp == end - 1` and `status == PARA_VALUE_QUOTED`. The vulnerable source checks only the parser state here; it does not test whether another byte exists before the next line inspects `tmp + 1`. The patch adds the missing `if(tmp+1>=end)` guard exactly at this point.

Sink. Because step 6 left `tmp` on the final backslash and there is no `tmp+1>=end` check, this expression dereferences the byte at `end`. ASan reports this exact read as a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at line 228, 0 bytes past the 17-byte fuzz buffer.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The patch adds `if(tmp+1>=end)` before the vulnerable escape read and before the opening-quote branch, which is the missing source-level guard for the witnessed trailing-backslash case, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

format.name: Compact SIP To header with quoted parameter trailing escape
format.contract: A parser-admitted SIP message that reaches a compact `T:` header whose parameter parser enters `PARA_VALUE_QUOTED` and then sees a backslash as the final byte of the available buffer. In the vulnerable source, once `parse_to_param` reaches `case '\\'` with `status == PARA_VALUE_QUOTED` and `tmp == end - 1`, the next line `switch(*(tmp + 1))` reads one byte past `end`. The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_38080/poc` is a 17-byte example satisfying that condition (sha256 `4a533f7db1f5acac622c49a8c5637a61d87f5e1264e00dcead3b0256aa97b534`).
